name: Compliance officer or regulator
oneLine: KYC, KYB, KYA, AML, consumer protection, AI rules.
goals: Map each party in an agent payment to an existing regulated role, or document the gap.
Define what Know Your Agent must mean in practice: who is accountable for an agent and what records exist.
Keep sanctions screening and AML monitoring working when the payer is a wallet address and the initiator is a model.
Protect consumers' rights to dispute, refund and revoke under Regulation E, Regulation Z, PSD2 and their successors.
Apply AI Act transparency obligations and record-keeping to agents that make purchases.
Produce audit evidence: who authorized what, when, with which constraints.
pains: Regulation E's definition of unauthorized transfer turns on whether the consumer furnished the access device, and delegation to an agent sits right on that line.
Stablecoin rules (the GENIUS Act and the OCC's first rule under it, both effective 2027-01-18, and MiCA) say nothing about agents, and facilitators that never hold funds fall between categories.
Agent registries record identifiers, not legal persons, and most entries are placeholders.

AP2 and Verifiable Intent produce signed mandates, but production use is thinly documented. Google says Gemini has used AP2 for purchases since 2026-11-17 (checkout with Google Pay in Tasks in Gemini, rolling out to US users aged 18 and over, in English), yet it has published no AP2 version, mandate type, signer or verifier, and no public source shows AP2 mandates exchanged with merchants, processors, credential providers or networks. Mastercard and its partners have announced two live purchases that used Verifiable Intent: a flight on 2026-11-12 and a coffee an agent bought on 2026-11-19, with acceptance supported by Antom. Neither protocol is shown in live use inside UCP, and no announcement says who verifies a mandate chain, so audit trails are inconsistent.
Consent is captured in different places (wallet, surface, merchant) with different retention rules.

Rules and guidance are still arriving, and as of 2026-11-21 no payments law or regulation in the jurisdictions covered here addresses agents directly: PSD3 and the PSR, which would replace PSD2, passed the Council at first reading on 2026-10-29 without an agent-specific provision and still await the European Parliament. The closest texts are proposals and plans. The European Commission's Digital Fairness Act proposal (2026-11-11) would require a business that offers consumers an agent that concludes contracts for them to have each consumer choose at first use whether to confirm all of the agent's purchases, only those that meet criteria the consumer sets, or none, and its agent rules do not apply to financial services; MAS said on 2026-11-19 that it will facilitate the development of a know-your-agent protocol for customer agents and financial institutions, with no specification or timeline yet. Elsewhere there is a Treasury letter, FCA priorities and speeches, an HM Treasury consultation still without a response, MAS guidelines, and no CFPB rule.
decisions: Whether agent-initiated transactions require their own consent, disclosure and record-keeping policy.
Which registries, attestations or certifications count as Know Your Agent evidence.
Sanctions and AML treatment of facilitators, relays and agent wallets.
How to apply unauthorized-transaction liability when a mandate existed.
